assignments.title: General equilibrium and welfare

canonical_specification.outcome: Analyze exchange and production interactions across markets.

owned_paths: content/projects/v05-c05-* (only if instruction actually needs an offline asset)
assignments.content: Define pure-exchange and production economies, commodity/endowment/ownership income, price normalization, individual optimization and aggregate feasibility. Explain Edgeworth-box coordinates and contract curve with a readable original static diagram or clear coordinate representation; derive a complete original two-consumer equilibrium with endogenous wealth and both market checks, Walras law and its omitted-positive-price qualification. Define Pareto efficiency versus distribution; prove the first welfare result at a clearly specified finite-economy scope, distinguishing convexity from its other assumptions. State the second welfare theorem with its actual convexity/support/transfer and equilibrium-versus-quasiequilibrium caveats; provide a constructive supporting-price/transfer example and an appropriate restricted proof rather than an unproved universal assertion. Include production interaction/ownership and missing-market limitations with a solved case. At least two fully worked examples (three if needed), eight complete solved exercises, proof/transfer/critique, teach-back and answered delayed check; source inspection and independent exact numerical checker. Do not claim general equilibrium existence/uniqueness or dynamic stability without proof; graduate global existence and full nonsmooth support extensions remain later.

assignments.title: Monopoly, oligopoly and pricing

canonical_specification.outcome: Solve market-power models and compare price and quantity competition.

owned_paths: content/projects/v05-c06-* (only if instruction actually needs an offline asset)
assignments.content: Derive profit-maximizing monopoly quantity/price from inverse demand and economic cost, global/corner/shutdown qualifications, MR and interior Lerner-elasticity condition with exact assumptions; explain deadweight loss versus transfers under the prior quasilinear welfare setup. Teach first-degree and third-degree discrimination with an original solved segmented-price case, no resale/observability/incentive constraints and welfare qualifications; introduce second-degree menus only conceptually and hand their IC derivation to c08/c09. Define the minimal simultaneous-action best-response/Nash concepts before deriving original Cournot duopoly quantities, profits and welfare, then show Bertrand homogeneous-good price competition with capacities, equal-cost/tie-rule/continuous-price hypotheses and deviation proof. Compare market definitions/product differentiation and entry barriers/fixed costs without claiming that any market structure is empirically identified by firm count. At least two fully worked examples (three if useful), eight fully solved exercises, proof/transfer/critique, teach-back and answered delayed check; source inspection and exact independent checker. c07 develops general game theory so do not assume its results as already taught.

assignments.title: Game theory and strategic behavior

canonical_specification.outcome: Identify equilibria and credible strategies in static and dynamic games.

owned_paths: content/projects/v05-c07-* (only if instruction actually needs an offline asset)
assignments.content: Define finite normal-form games, actions versus complete contingent strategies, payoffs/information/timing and common knowledge as assumptions. Strict versus weak dominance and deletion caveats; best responses and Nash equilibrium with full deviation inequalities, inefficient/multiple/no-pure examples. Derive mixed strategy probabilities by making the opponent indifferent, check support and off-support deviations, distinguish a belief/probability from a deterministic compromise; give finite mixed existence as a precisely scoped theorem with clear proof-route limits rather than claiming a full fixed-point proof. Define extensive form, histories/information sets, subgames, sequential rationality and subgame-perfect equilibrium. Solve an original observed-action entry/commitment game by backward induction, show a noncredible Nash threat and why irreversible commitment changes the game/payoffs; mention repeated-game horizon/monitoring limits only if pedagogically needed. At least two full worked examples, eight complete solved exercises incl proof/transfer/critique, teach-back and answered delayed check. Primary method content inspection and independent exact payoff/deviation/tree checks. This chapter is complete-information core; c08 teaches private types, Bayes updating and signaling equilibrium.

assignments.title: Information, signaling and selection

canonical_specification.outcome: Explain how asymmetric information changes trade and incentives.

owned_paths: content/projects/v05-c08-* (only if instruction actually needs an offline asset)
assignments.content: Teach hidden pre-contract types/adverse selection versus hidden actions/moral hazard, information sets and selection-conditioned beliefs. Derive an original competitive lemons market including pooling candidate consistency, composition changes and no-trade/equilibrium branches; avoid equating all private information with market failure. Build a two-type costly signaling model with competitive receiver wages/beliefs, Bayes rule on path, sequential incentives, pooling/separating outcomes and off-path-belief qualifications; explain education as a signal versus productivity and why equilibrium need not identify causality. Teach screening menus and self-selection through an original two-type IC/IR calculation and information rent, distinguishing signaling from screening and noting later contract extensions. Two or more full worked examples, eight complete solved exercises incl transfer/critique, teach-back and answered delayed check, inspected primary source routes and independent exact checker. Root owns shared acceptance, source merging, build/verify and hosting.
